newsitem.title: THAILAND: Caltex to change Asia focus, review Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Caltex to change Asia focus, review Cambodia.

text.p: Caltex Petroleum Corp said on Wednesday it will shift its focus in Asia to downstream marketing and planned to invest less in the refining business.

The multinational will also slow down investment in Cambodia following the eruption of factional fighting there, pending a reassessment of the political situation there, Jock McKenzie, its regional vice president told Reuters.
"Caltex's investment in Cambodia is worth about $20 million. Rather small compared to the overall portfolio," he said.

"If anything, we will probably slow down the investment. It's a bit early now to make final judgement as it's not really that clear what would be the ultimate outcome of the political upheaval there," he said.
Richard Abrams, managing director of Caltex Oil (Thailand), said the company will invest $200 million in Thailand over the next five years, mostly on downstream petroleum marketing.
Abrams said despite the sharp downturn in the economy, Caltex was confident that oil demand in Thailand would improve in the next 24 months as the economic crisis cleared.
"We view the current situation as temporary. Thailand will emerge stronger," he said.
The company welcomed the government's move not to control domestic oil prices after the de facto baht devaluation last week which saw the currency fall by more than 20 percent.
The Thai government on Tuesday decided to allow oil prices to rise to reflect the new foreign exchange rate. However, it asked oil companies to raise the prices in stages.
Caltex Petroleum Corp is owned jointly by U.S. producers and refiners Texaco Inc and Chevron Corp.
